headline: SILVER HITS YEARLY LOW BELOW $47.50 — Hawkish Fed and Rising Yields Drive XAG/USD to Worst Level Since December 2025
snippet: Silver hit a yearly low of US$47.34/oz on November 16 as the dollar surged to a 19-month high and 10-year Treasury yields held at 5.15%, with CME markets pricing a 94% chance of a December Fed rate hike — a move that takes the metal 60% below its January 2026 all-time high. FXStreet analysts watch $47.00–$47.50 as the technical zone where structural industrial demand from solar and EV sectors should provide a floor, with a weekly close below $47 signalling a deeper correction toward $44.

headline: HAMMER FALLS TODAY — Austral-Hammer Copper Scheme Legally Effective Nov 16; Final Implementation Nov 25
snippet: The Federal Court approved the Austral Resources–Hammer Metals scheme of arrangement on November 13, and the deal became legally effective today, November 16, with final implementation targeted for November 25. The acquisition consolidates Austral's position in Queensland's Mt Isa copper corridor, adding Hammer's exploration ground to Austral's existing copper processing infrastructure.

headline: GOLD $3,879 AS WARSH SPEAKS MONDAY — Retail Sales Tuesday, FOMC Minutes Wednesday Set the Week's Binary
snippet: Gold closed the week at US$3,879/oz after a 4.5% decline as the week-ahead data calendar sets up a clear binary: hotter-than-expected US retail sales on Tuesday would reinforce the 94% December hike probability and test $3,800 support, while a soft print could relieve pressure and open a path back toward $4,000. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Monday speech is the first intraday catalyst, with any hawkish surprise likely to accelerate selling before the data prints.

headline: YUKON METALS DRILLS 33.40 g/t GOLD Over 1.0m at Birch; Second Hole Returns 30.8m of Copper-Gold
snippet: Yukon Metals Corp. reported that drill hole BK26-003 at the 100%-owned Birch Project in Yukon intersected 1.0 metre grading 33.40 g/t gold, with a second hole in the program also returning a broad zone of 30.8 metres at 0.17% copper and 0.14 g/t gold. The results confirm the project's high-grade gold and porphyry copper-gold character, with both holes from the 2026 exploration campaign.

headline: ABEN GOLD Opens 2026 Campaign — First Justin Hole Returns 7.55m at 0.392% TUNGSTEN, a Critical Mineral Few Explorers Are Chasing
snippet: Aben Gold (TSX-V: ABM) reported first assay results from its 2026 drill program at the Justin Gold-Tungsten Project in Yukon, with hole JN26-003 returning 7.55 metres at 0.392% tungsten including a 0.87-metre sub-interval at 0.087% W. Tungsten was added to both the US and Canadian critical minerals lists in 2026, bringing new strategic demand context to a project that has historically been evaluated primarily for its gold potential.

headline: BARRICK MAINTAINS HERCULES POSITION — World's No. 2 Gold Miner Subscribes for 6.6M New Shares to Preserve Anti-Dilution Rights
snippet: Barrick Mining Corporation (NYSE: B, TSX: ABX) exercised its anti-dilution rights under an existing investor agreement with Hercules Metals Corp., subscribing for approximately 6.638 million common shares to maintain its strategic position following a recent Hercules equity raise. The move from the world's second-largest gold producer signals continued confidence in Hercules' British Columbia gold exploration portfolio and is a noteworthy vote of conviction from a major at a time when junior gold equities are broadly under pressure.

headline: EX-CHINA RARE EARTHS REBOUND — SMM Weekly: Light REE Prices Broadly Up; Dysprosium, Terbium Extend November Gains
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's November 15 ex-China weekly rare earth review showed light rare earth prices broadly raised as intensive regional supply chain moves accelerated outside China, with heavy rare earths dysprosium and terbium also extending their November gains. The rebound follows weeks of pressure from Chinese export quota uncertainty, and market participants are closely watching Beijing's December policy announcements for signals on 2027 export allowances.

headline: GOLD, COPPER AT MULTI-MONTH LOWS — Sector Sells Off as AI Trade Fades and Rate Fear Returns to Mining
snippet: Mining Stock Daily's morning briefing reports gold and copper futures are both at multi-month lows as the mining sector absorbs two compounding forces: AI-equity selling has reduced risk appetite broadly, while elevated Treasury yields at 5.15% are compressing gold's opportunity cost and signalling continued margin pressure on base metal producers. The combined effect has pushed major gold producers to multi-year valuation lows relative to spot metal prices — a dynamic that historically precedes mean reversion when the rate catalyst shifts.

headline: MINERS SET TO RETURN 2-3X BULLION — Franklin Templeton Sees Leveraged Upside; OCBC Targets $4,600 Gold by Year-End
snippet: A Franklin Templeton strategist argues that gold mining stocks are positioned to return two to three times what physical bullion does in the next precious metals rally, since producers gain from both higher metal prices and margin expansion as cost inflation normalises. OCBC's precious metals analyst separately targets US$4,600/oz gold by end of 2026, implying approximately 18% upside from current levels and significant operational leverage for producers with all-in sustaining costs below $2,000/oz.

headline: IGO'S NOVA NICKEL MINE CLOSES WITH PRODUCTION BEAT — 21,340t Beats Guidance by 7%; Site Pivots to Lithium Under Global Lithium Resources
snippet: IGO Limited's Nova nickel-copper-cobalt mine in Western Australia completed its final production run, delivering 21,340 tonnes of nickel — 7% above the top of its revised guidance range — with cash costs 8% below guidance at A$3.90 per pound of payable nickel. Global Lithium Resources is acquiring the Nova site and plans to repurpose its existing processing infrastructure to advance the Manna lithium project, shifting the asset's strategic focus from nickel to battery-grade lithium at a time when Western lithium processing capacity remains scarce.
